leversOnTheBaseline.clientField: src/lib/multiplayer/client.ts:1123 - `pendingIntentCount: state.pendingIntents.size`; the map is written at :1336 on every sent intent and cleared ONLY by settlePendingIntent (:1377-1380), which is called from the Event handler when payload.intentId matches (:349-352) and from the Error handler (:394).
leversOnTheBaseline.lever: a new `dropNextIntent()` arm on the EXISTING per-page transport harness in this file (installLifecycleHarness, e2e/gm-two-player-lifecycle.pack.spec.ts:336-422): swallow the guest page's next client->server frame whose `kind` is `Intent` inside route.onMessage (:355-365). The client keeps the entry in pendingIntents, the server never sees the frame, and no receipt can ever carry its intentId - so the posture is PERMANENT rather than a one-round-trip transient.
leversOnTheBaseline.leverProvenance: the arm is lifted from .sisyphus/roadmap-completion-20260912/u1e-row-b.patch, which is U1c's own seven-posture build; U1c's local receipt records that both row-B arms were driven green there before the split.
leversOnTheBaseline.stability: permanent by construction. Nothing in client.ts removes a pendingIntents entry for an intent the server never received. Row B asserts that persistence explicitly (a re-read one second after the capture) so a transient pending between some other intent and its receipt cannot be mistaken for the driven one.
leversOnTheBaseline.existingLiveRow: NONE - see R0 below for the captured grep. No assertion anywhere in e2e/ reads or renders `pending`.
leversOnTheBaseline.gap: no rendered data-state, no rendered announcement, no rendered gating assertion for pending anywhere

leversOnTheBaseline.derivation: src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalLifecycleState.ts:189 - `if (input.client.blockedBySequenceCollision) return 'blocked';`, precedence 1 of 10, so it outranks the pending the row is already holding
leversOnTheBaseline.clientField: src/lib/multiplayer/client.ts:897 - `if (known !== identity) state.blockedBySequenceCollision = true;` inside admitByDelivery, reached when a delivery sequence at or below lastAppliedDelivery arrives carrying a DIFFERENT event identity (identityOf, :995-1002, is the event's own `id`). The flag is written in exactly one place and cleared in none: `grep -n blockedBySequenceCollision src/lib/multiplayer/client.ts` = :67 (public field), :162 (state field), :341/:379 (the PROTOCOL_VIOLATION emit edges), :611 (constructed false), :881 (admission short-circuit), :897 (the single write), :1122 (projection). Terminal by construction.
leversOnTheBaseline.lever: a new `collideNextDelivery()` arm on the same harness: on the next server->client frame carrying a numeric `deliverySequence`, forward the REAL frame and then a twin of it whose `event.id` is prefixed `collision-`. The first is applied and remembered (rememberApplied, client.ts:356); the twin then satisfies `deliverySequence <= state.lastAppliedDelivery` with a known-but-different identity and sets the flag. No refusal code is invented - the frame is a duplicate of one the server actually sent.

gateSurface.whatIsAsserted: src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalCommandGate.ts:60-72 tacticalCommandAvailability, whose refused set is exactly the six keys of GATE_REASONS (:37-48) - blocked, rebuilding, rewound, syncing, reconnecting, behind - and whose reason string reaches the player through `aria-describedby` at src/components/multiplayer/NetworkedGameSurface.actionContext.ts:90 pointing at NETWORKED_ACTION_REFUSAL_ID (:22).
gateSurface.whereItRenders: src/components/multiplayer/NetworkedGameSurface.actionbar.tsx:226-229 - `if (context.refusalReason === null) return null;` then a single sr-only span with that id. So the node's PRESENCE is the gate's answer and its text is the gate's reason, which is why row A reads presence plus text and row B does the same.
gateSurface.rowBSignificance: pending is NOT a GATE_REASONS key and blocked IS. Row B is therefore the first row anywhere that exercises the gate in BOTH directions on postures whose gating has never been rendered: the player's own in-flight command must stay playable, and a collided stream must refuse.
gateSurface.notCommandsEnabled: posture.commandsEnabled (tacticalLifecycleState.ts:147) is false for pending AND blocked and is rendered nowhere. The divergence is deliberate (tacticalCommandGate.ts:11-24). Row B asserts the rendered surface, as row A did, and says so at the call site.
gateSurface.banner:
src/components/multiplayer/TacticalLifecycleStateBanner.tsx:30-43 - one

{posture.message}

. The announcement contract is structural and identical in every posture; the per-posture half is that the announced CONTENT was this posture's own sentence.

distinctnessStrategy.obligation: pairwise-distinct messages against EVERY row-A posture (live, sealed, finalized, syncing, behind) and against each other.
distinctnessStrategy.chosen: row B captures its two sentences LIVE off the banner, then compares them against the five row-A messages obtained through the product's own exported derivation, deriveTacticalLifecyclePosture (tacticalLifecycleState.ts:139-156). Row A used the mirror image of this - it derived row B's two messages and pinned them against the five it drove live (row A :210-223).
distinctnessStrategy.whyNotReDriveRowA: the brief forbids re-driving the row-A postures beyond what distinctness needs, and re-driving them would double the row's wall time and duplicate five arms that already pass in row A on every run of this same group. The derivation is the product's own message table, not a copy of it, so the comparison cannot drift from what the banner would render.
distinctnessStrategy.soundnessBinding: the comparison is only meaningful if the rendered text and the derived message are the same string for a driven posture. Row B asserts exactly that for its own two - rendered text === derived message for pending and for blocked - which is what licenses comparing a derived row-A message against a rendered row-B one.
distinctnessStrategy.teeth: the seven-member set (5 derived row-A + 2 rendered row-B) must have seven distinct members. LIFECYCLE_TONE (src/lib/lifecycle/lifecycleState.ts:60-71) gives behind/rewound/rebuilding ONE palette triple and pending/syncing/reconnecting another, so colour cannot separate pending from syncing; the sentence is the only thing that can.

reconnecting - reconnectScheduled is a real client field and deriveState maps it (tacticalLifecycleState.ts:202), but no available lever renders it; U1c measured three levers with a MutationObserver recording every transition and the series steps straight to behind. rebuilding - a pure function of a correction lease no in-paths lever acquires (src/lib/events/journal/EventHistoryDurableRebuild.ts:45-59). Carried from U1c.
row B does not re-drive live, sealed, finalized, syncing or behind. Their sentences enter row B only through the product's own derivation, for the distinctness obligation.

redPlan.R1: M-A applied (remove `blocked` from GATE_REASONS, src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalCommandGate.ts) -> full E2E build -> `--group=lifecycle-pack` on the SHIPPED one-row spec. The mutation is permissive-only, so it cannot break an unrelated pack by making something MORE available; tsc stays at 0 because GatedTacticalState is keyof typeof GATE_REASONS (the same invisibility U1c measured for its M3).

risksForTheParent.risk: the pending lever needs the GUEST to be the side the turn-ownership gate opens, because advancePhase (e2e/helpers/gmTwoPlayerMatchFlow.ts:117-146) clicks whichever surface has an enabled control and only the guest page is routed through the harness.
risksForTheParent.mitigation: the arm is set BEFORE the drive and the drive is a bounded loop (8 attempts, 500ms apart) that re-reads the posture between advances, so it fires on the guest's next intent whenever the rotation reaches it and fails loudly naming the last posture otherwise. Not a widening: the loop lives in e2e/.
risksForTheParent.escalatesIf: eight advances pass without the guest ever acting - then the lever, not the unit, is wrong and the parent is told rather than the row being weakened.

risksForTheParent.risk: the blocked arm wedges the client that receives it - a collided client self-pauses and its phase control can detach mid-click.
risksForTheParent.mitigation: the same bounded drive tolerates a failed click and keeps reading the posture, exactly as the held patch does; a genuinely stuck drive still runs out of attempts and throws.

risksForTheParent.risk: extending the shared harness could change row A's behaviour.
risksForTheParent.mitigation: both arms are disarmed at construction and row A never calls them; the three green two-row runs with identical captured lists are the measurement. If row A's captured list changes at all, that is a blocker and the parent is told.
